answer.policy_title: Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal CMM-312: Knee Surgery-Arthroscopic and Open Procedures
criteria_quotes: 29881 — Arthroscopy, knee, surgical; with meniscectomy (medial OR lateral, including any meniscal shaving) including debridement/shaving of articular cartilage (chondroplasty), same or separate compartment(s), when performed.
Symptoms include function-limiting knee pain and/or loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment.
Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration.

Provider-directed non-surgical management may include, but is not limited to, ice, relative rest or activity modification, acupuncture, weight loss, supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises, prescription or non-prescription medications, assistive devices, and intra-articular injections.
answer.appeal_deadline: The appeal must be received by 2027-02-18, which is 180 days after the 2026-08-22 denial notice date.
answer.submission_route: First call Cigna Customer Service at the telephone number on the back of the Cigna ID card and state that you want to appeal the adverse coverage determination. Submit the Cigna Customer Appeal Request form or a written appeal letter with the denial notice, reference number POC-58F5CA7616-94713, clinical records, imaging reports, and the treating clinician's statement. The Cigna form states that the mailing address depends on the ID card: for a Cigna Network card, mail to Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8011; for a card showing GW-Cigna or a G, mail to Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188062, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8062. Use the address applicable to the card, not both addresses.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Ask Cigna Customer Service and the provider who submitted the prior-authorization request for the complete clinical review criteria actually used for this denial, including the applicable CMM-312 version, any Cigna CPT code list or delegated-vendor criteria, and the clinical rationale for applying the criteria. The Cigna policy states that some plans may use delegated-vendor guidelines and that the member's specific plan document controls if it conflicts with the policy. Request the criteria in writing and cite reference number POC-58F5CA7616-94713. The Cigna Customer Appeal Request form also permits submission of the denial letter and medical records supporting medical necessity.

The retrieved policy states that Cigna coverage policies are guidance and that the applicable benefit plan and any delegated-vendor criteria may control. The quoted symptom and three-month conservative-treatment language was publicly retrieved in the indexed CMM-312 guideline material; the patient should request the exact clinical-review worksheet or criteria version used in this individual determination before relying on it as the complete denial standard.

Autologous Chondrocyte Implantation (ACI) or Autologous Chondrocyte Transplantation (ACT) a cell-based cartilage repair surgical technique that utilizes an individual's own cells in an effort to repair damage to articular cartilage with the goal of improving joint function and reducing pain. The procedure involves the collection and culture of articular cartilage cells (i.e., chondrocytes) that are then implanted into the cartilage defect with the intent that the cultured cells will contribute to the regeneration and repair of the articular surface. • Hybrid Autologous Chondrocyte Implantation (ACI): ACI is combined with other surgical repair techniques of cartilage defects (e.g., osteochondral autograft transfer). MACI® Implant (Matrix Induced Autologous Chondrocyte Implant) received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration December 2016 as an autologous cellularized scaffold indicated for repair of single or multiple symptomatic, full-thickness cartilage defects of the knee with or without bone involvement in adults.
